newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's VDA sees '97 car registrations up 1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Germany's VDA sees '97 car registrations up 1 pct.

text.p: Germany's automobile industry association (VDA) expects new car registrations to rise this year by one percent, accelerating to three percent in 1998, VDA chief executive Kunibert Schmidt said on Tuesday.
Schmidt told Saarland radio registrations had fallen five percent in the first five months of this year, but he expected sales to pick up to show net growth for 1997 as a whole.
For 1998 "the domestic market will be significantly above the zero line", he said in extracts released from an interview.

Schmidt warned, however, that car industry prospects depended heavily on whether the Bonn government decides to hike petrol taxes to help the government finance tax reforms and cut borrowing to qualify for Europe's single currency.

"Our positive expectations for the second half of this year and next year depended strongly on what happens on the tax front in Bonn," Schmidt said, adding that a VDA survey had shown that three-quarters of Germans opposed a petrol tax hike.
